messages:
maria: quick thread — saw a customer hit weird residency mismatches after a proxy rotation. session stayed sticky but backend affinity moved regions, so writes were rejected by legal checks. anyone seen this pattern?
ajay: yep, seen it once during canary. the proxy rotation rebalanced sticky slots without preserving the residency stamp.
leila: is this the new rotation mode where we round-robin sidecars instead of draining?
samir: correct — stage-3 rotation (fast-rotate) trades a drain for speed. it assumes client hints + idempotency. apparently not safe when residency is enforced server-side.
maria: root cause seems to be that sticky-session key -> proxy instance mapping persisted, but the proxy instance's backing region tag changed during the rotation (k8s node move). client sent sticky cookie, hit proxy that's now backed by a different region.
ajay: short term mitigation: reject fast-rotate when any tenant has residency flag == STRICT. fallback to drain mode for those tenants.
leila: agree. long term: we should propagate an immutable residency token in the session cookie, not just rely on instance tags. e.g., set X-Region-Stamp or an encoded lease.
samir: note: stamped cookie needs replay protection and mustn't leak PII. if we encode region claim, it should be ephemeral and signed by control plane (TTL ~ 5m).
maria: proposal: introduce header 'x-residency-lease: <signed-blob>' issued by control plane. proxies validate lease locally (sig + ttl) and refuse to accept if lease region != backing region. control plane issues swap leases during controlled handoffs.
ajay: sounds reasonable. tradeoffs: extra crypto on hot path, more control-plane ops to issue leases at scale. can we cache verification keys in proxies and rotate keys infrequently?
samir: yes — proxies cache public keys. verification is lightweight (ed25519). cost should be negligible compared to token parsing + auth.
leila: operationally we need: 1) lease issuance API, 2) key-rotation CLI, 3) observability (lease-mismatch counter, lease-expiry traces).
maria: also need a fallback: if proxy can't validate lease due to key missing, what's the default? fall back to deny (safe) or allow (availability)? legal prefers deny. ops prefers allow. propose config per cluster: default-deny for EU clusters.
ajay: can we do hybrid: if tenant has legal_flag STRICT -> deny; else allow with audit log.
samir: agree. add a canary mode where we log mismatches for 24h and then flip policy.
sre-bot: Canary test results: canary rotation (fast-rotate) on staging-3 caused 0.3% residency-mismatch errors; rollback initiated automatically.
leila: next steps I suggest: 1) add draft RFC for "residency leases" (interface + signature scheme + TTLs), 2) short-term RBAC fix: mark tenants with STRICT -> force drain rotations, 3) add telemetry dashboard for mismatch rate.
maria: I'll start the RFC draft and include a minimal sequence diagram. I'll also open a quick ops PR to force-drain with tenant-residency check.
ajay: I can prototype the ed25519 verification in the proxy runtime (small lib). estimate 2d.
samir: I'll scope the control-plane lease-issuer API and load testing. also will write runbook steps for operator rollback if we hit false denies.
leila: ping me when RFC is up — I'll add compliance/legal review notes about what qualifies as "region" and acceptable TTLs.
maria: thanks — setting action items: RFC (maria), proxy lib prototype (ajay), control-plane API + runbook (samir), compliance review (leila). I'll post back in 48h with RFC link. :thumbsup:
